text: I think the first piece is that you absolutely need to have one, to start by saying that. Regardless of what level you are in the company.
speaker: Ebi Atawodi
context: Lenny asks Ebi about the elements of a good vision for a product or company. Ebi emphasizes that every product manager, regardless of their level, needs to have some form of vision - whether micro or macro. She uses the analogy of getting on a plane where the pilot doesn't know the destination to illustrate why having a clear vision is essential for any PM role.
text_ko: 제일 먼저, 시작할 때 ‘이건 꼭 있어야 한다’고 분명히 말하는 게 필요하다고 생각해요. 회사에서 어떤 직급에 있든 상관없어요.
text_zh: 我觉得第一点就是，你肯定得有一个，先把这个说清楚。不管你在公司是什么级别。
text_es: Creo que lo primero es que sí o sí necesitas tener uno, empezando por decir eso. No importa en qué nivel de la empresa estés.
key_sentence: You need a micro macro vision, regardless of what level you are.
original_text: I think the first piece is that you absolutely need to have one, to start by saying that. Regardless of what level you are in the company. So people say, "Oh, I'm just a junior PM." Whatever level, there is some micro macro vision that you need to have. Because essentially if you got on a plane and the pilot was like, "I don't really know where we're going, but I'm a really good pilot. The company needs to fly 400 flights this year. So I'm trying to make that happen, but trust me, we'll get there."

vocabulary.definition: Without considering or being affected by something; despite the circumstances.
vocabulary.businessContext: In professional discussions, 'regardless' is often used to emphasize the importance of a point or action that should be taken irrespective of other factors.
vocabulary.nuance: This term can sometimes imply a dismissal of potential obstacles, so it should be used carefully to avoid sounding dismissive of valid concerns.

vocabulary.definition: A specific stage or degree of progress, achievement, or rank within a hierarchy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, 'level' is frequently used to describe positions within an organizational structure, indicating seniority or expertise.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can also imply a sense of equality or parity when discussing teams or individuals, so context is important to clarify its intended meaning.

text: The first one is it needs to be lofty. So it needs to be something that feels... It almost scares you in an exciting way, right? Like, oh, my God, this is something I can get up every morning. And if we did that, goddamn.
speaker: Ebi Atawodi
context: Ebi explains the key elements of a good product vision. She describes how a vision should balance being inspiring and ambitious (lofty) while still feeling achievable. The vision should excite and motivate people to work toward it every day, but not be so unrealistic that it feels impossible to reach.
text_ko: 첫 번째는 목표가 높아야 해요. 거의 겁이 날 정도로 설레는 느낌이어야 해요. '아, 세상에, 이건 내가 매일 아침 일어나서 하고 싶은 일이야' 하고 느껴질 만큼요. 그걸 해낸다면, 와, 정말 끝내줄 거예요.
text_zh: 第一个要求就是目标要定得高远。得让人感觉...怎么说呢，就是那种既兴奋又有点怕怕的感觉，对吧？就像"天哪，这事儿真让我每天早上都想爬起来干活。要是真做成了，那可太牛了。"
text_es: La primera es que tiene que ser ambiciosa. O sea, tiene que ser algo que se sienta... que casi te dé miedo pero de la manera emocionante, ¿no? Como que dices "hostia, esto es algo por lo que me puedo levantar cada mañana. Y si logramos esto, joder."
key_sentence: It needs to be something that feels... It almost scares you in an exciting way.
original_text: The first one is it needs to be lofty. So it needs to be something that feels... It almost scares you in an exciting way, right? Like, oh, my God, this is something I can get up every morning. And if we did that, goddamn. But at the same time, it needs to be realistic and attainable, so it cannot feel so pie in the sky that it feels so out of reach, right?

vocabulary.definition: Of imposing height; also, having high ideals or ambitions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'lofty' often describes goals or visions that are ambitious and aspirational, pushing the boundaries of what is considered achievable.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'lofty' conveys a sense of grandeur, it can also imply impracticality if not grounded in reality.

text: So I have a very simplistic framework. I actually don't know who put it together at Uber, but I see as well, one of the most powerful skills of a product manager is storytelling, right?
speaker: Ebi Atawodi
context: Lenny asks Ebi about what a vision looks like concretely as a document. Ebi introduces her storytelling framework for creating product visions, emphasizing that storytelling is one of the most powerful skills for product managers. She explains that throughout history, stories have been more memorable and impactful than numbers or statistics for communicating ideas.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 아주 단순한 프레임워크(framework)가 있어요. 사실 그걸 우버에서 누가 만든 건지는 잘 모르겠어요. 다만 제가 보기에는 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)의 가장 강력한 역량 중 하나가 스토리텔링(storytelling)인 것 같아요, 그렇죠?
text_zh: 我的框架其实很简单。说实话我也不知道是Uber的谁总结出来的，但我觉得产品经理最重要的一个能力就是会讲故事，对吧？
text_es: Entonces tengo un marco súper sencillo. La verdad no sé quién lo armó en Uber, pero veo que una de las habilidades más poderosas de un product manager es saber contar historias, ¿no?
key_sentence: Storytelling is one of the most powerful skills of a product manager.
original_text: So I have a very simplistic framework. I actually don't know who put it together at Uber, but I see as well, one of the most powerful skills of a product manager is storytelling, right? Because you look at generation after generation after generation, what people pass on as stories, they're not numbers, they're not stats, it's stories.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides guidance and support for understanding or addressing a particular issue or task.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a framework often refers to a set of guidelines or principles that help teams develop strategies, processes, or products effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'framework' suggests a supportive structure, it can imply rigidity; thus, it is important to ensure flexibility within the framework to adapt to changing circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: Having great strength, influence, or effectiveness; capable of producing significant results or impacts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, describing a skill or tool as 'powerful' indicates its potential to drive success, enhance productivity, or influence decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'powerful' can carry a positive connotation of effectiveness but may also suggest a level of intimidation or overwhelming force in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: The art of conveying information or messages through narratives, often to engage, inform, or persuade an audience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, storytelling is used in marketing, branding, and leadership to create emotional connections with customers and stakeholders, making messages more relatable and memorable.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'storytelling' is generally viewed positively, it is essential to ensure that the narratives are authentic and not overly embellished, as this can lead to mistrust.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and feature definition of a product, acting as a liaison between various stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers play a crucial role in guiding product development, ensuring that the final product meets market needs and aligns with business objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The role of a product manager can vary significantly between organizations, with some requiring a more technical background while others may focus on market analysis and customer engagement.

text: I think too many people lean into and, "Let's go test it, let's go do some research." It's like, dude, you're a human. Look at the products. Would you use that? You built some intuition from just exposing yourself to really good products.
speaker: Ebi Atawodi
context: Ebi discusses the 'empathize' step of developing a vision, specifically talking about how product managers should approach understanding user problems. She argues that PMs often over-rely on formal research when they should trust their own intuition as users. She advocates for 'dog-fooding' (using your own product) and 'cat-fooding' (using competitors' products) as essential practices.
text_ko: 사람들이 너무 ‘테스트해보자, 리서치하자’ 쪽으로만 치우치는 것 같아요. 솔직히 그냥 사람인데요. 제품을 한 번 보면 이걸 내가 쓸지 말지가 보여요. 좋은 제품들을 많이 접해보기만 해도 직관(intuition)이 생겨요.
text_zh: 我觉得太多人一上来就说"咱们去测试一下，做点调研吧。" 兄弟，你也是人啊，看看这些产品，你自己会用吗？多接触一些真正好的产品，你自然就有感觉了。
text_es: Creo que mucha gente se va demasiado por el "vamos a probarlo, vamos a investigar un poco". Es como, oye, eres una persona normal. Mira los productos. ¿Los usarías tú? Desarrollas intuición simplemente exponiéndote a productos realmente buenos.
key_sentence: Would you use that? You built some intuition from just exposing yourself to really good products.
original_text: I think too many people lean into and, "Let's go test it, let's go do some research." It's like, dude, you're a human. Look at the products. Would you use that? You built some intuition from just exposing yourself to really good products. Every time you pick up your phone, what is it about the apps that you love?

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup world, intuition often guides entrepreneurs in making quick decisions based on their experiences and gut feelings about market trends.
vocabulary.nuance: Intuition is often seen as a valuable asset in business, but it should be balanced with data-driven analysis to avoid potential pitfalls.

vocabulary.definition: The act of making something visible or known, especially something that was previously hidden or unknown.
vocabulary.businessContext: Exposing oneself to various products and market trends can enhance a business leader's understanding of consumer preferences and innovation opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: Exposing can carry a negative connotation if it involves revealing sensitive information or vulnerabilities, so context is important.

text: If I could put all the research into Bard or ChatGPT and it could spit out a PRD, then you haven't done your job. So basically I maybe panicked my team.
speaker: Ebi Atawodi
context: Lenny and Ebi discuss the importance of product managers developing their own judgment rather than just following research data. Ebi challenges her team to think about what unique value they provide that AI cannot replicate. She emphasizes that if an AI could do a PM's job by simply processing research, then the PM isn't adding sufficient human insight and product sense to their role.
text_ko: 만약 제가 모든 리서치를 Bard나 ChatGPT에 넣기만 하면 PRD(제품 요구사항 문서)가 뚝딱 나온다면, 그건 당신이 일을 제대로 안 한 거예요. 그래서 어쩌면 저는 팀을 좀 당황하게 만들었을 수도 있어요.
text_zh: 如果我把所有调研资料丢给Bard或者ChatGPT，它们就能直接输出一份产品需求文档(PRD)的话，那说明你们根本没做好自己的工作。所以基本上我可能把团队给吓着了。
text_es: Si pudiera meter toda la investigación en Bard o ChatGPT y que me escupiera un PRD, entonces no has hecho bien tu trabajo. Así que básicamente creo que asusté a mi equipo.
original_text: If I could put all the research into Bard or ChatGPT and it could spit out a PRD, then you haven't done your job. So basically I maybe panicked my team. I came in, I'm like, gen AI, everybody's talking about all the stuff that you do with creating content, but what I want you to think about is what is the value add you bring that I can't just put into an AI right now and say, "Tell me the big thing based on this research that exists."

text: I do not believe in being liked. I believe in being loved, right? And that's a very, very different thing. When I said this once in a meeting, people were like... Yes, right?
speaker: Ebi Atawodi
context: Ebi explains her philosophy about team relationships and leadership. She distinguishes between being 'liked' versus being 'loved' in a professional context. She defines love as choosing to extend yourself for someone else's growth, which sometimes means having difficult conversations rather than just being nice or agreeable. This philosophy guides how she approaches feedback and team management.
text_ko: 저는 사람들이 저를 좋아해 주는 것에는 신경 안 써요. 저는 사랑받는 걸 더 중요하게 생각해요, 알죠? 이건 완전히 다른 얘기예요. 예전에 회의에서 이렇게 말했더니 사람들 반응이… '맞아요, 그렇죠?' 이런 식이었어요.
text_zh: 我不追求让人喜欢，我追求的是让人真心认可，对吧？这完全是两码事。我有一次在会上这么说，大家都是这个反应...没错吧？
text_es: No creo en caer bien. Yo creo en que te amen, ¿me explico? Y eso es algo muy, muy diferente. Cuando dije esto una vez en una junta, la gente se quedó como... Sí, ¿verdad?
key_sentence: I do not believe in being liked; I believe in being loved.
original_text: I do not believe in being liked. I believe in being loved, right? And that's a very, very different thing. When I said this once in a meeting, people were like... Yes, right? But it took me a while in reading a lot of books to come to a definition of love and love is the choice to extend yourself for the spiritual growth of oneself or another, right?
